title: Trump: Whistleblower Reality Winner is arrested for releasing report on Russian interference
description_short: Trump: Whistleblower Reality Winner is arrested for releasing report on Russian interference
description_medium: Reality Winner, a former National Security Agency contractor, was arrested in June 2017 and charged under the Espionage Act after a classified report about Russian interference in the 2016 election was disclosed to the press. The document reportedly described attempts to access voter-registration systems. The prosecution and the report’s accuracy are separate questions.
description_long: Reality Winner, a former National Security Agency contractor, was arrested in June 2017 and charged under the Espionage Act after a classified report about Russian election interference was disclosed to the press. The report was described as covering Russian efforts to access voter-registration data. The Justice Department pursued the case while Donald Trump was president, and Winner remained imprisoned when he left office in January 2021. The prosecution brought attention to how the government handles unauthorized disclosures of classified information and how the public learns about election-security threats. A criminal charge is an allegation, and the fact of prosecution does not establish that every claim in the disclosed report was accurate. Without the full report and trial evidence, the details of the underlying cyber activity and the scope of Winner’s disclosure cannot be assessed. The event is the arrest and prosecution of Winner over the disclosure, with the report’s contents and the government’s case kept distinct.

title: Trump: 12 Russia GRU agents indicted for hacking and 2016 election interference
description_short: Trump: 12 Russia GRU agents indicted for hacking and 2016 election interference
description_medium: On July 13, 2018, Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein announced indictments against 12 officers of Russia’s GRU. Prosecutors accused them of hacking Democratic and campaign-related systems during the 2016 election; an indictment is an allegation, not a conviction. The defendants were charged, not convicted, in the announcement.
description_long: Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein announced on July 13, 2018, that a federal grand jury had indicted 12 members of Russia’s military intelligence agency, the GRU. Special Counsel Robert Mueller’s team charged them with conspiring to hack computers belonging to Americans and U.S. organizations connected to the 2016 election. The indictment described alleged intrusions into Democratic Party systems and the theft and release of campaign materials. The announcement made a specific attribution to Russian military intelligence through a formal criminal charging document. It did not mean the defendants had appeared in U.S. court or been convicted; the charges were allegations by prosecutors. The event occurred while Trump was president and as Russian interference remained politically central. The indictment set out prosecutors’ charges but did not resolve every question about election influence or contacts with U.S. campaigns.

title: Donald Trump is sent to hospital for ‘a series of mini-strokes'
description_short: Donald Trump is sent to hospital for ‘a series of mini-strokes'
description_medium: Donald Trump made an unscheduled visit to Walter Reed in November 2019 and later said it was part of his annual physical. A 2020 book revived mini-stroke claims, but no medical record or verified diagnosis supports them. The hospital visit itself cannot establish a diagnosis. The visit does not confirm the rumor.

title: Trump: FBI abuses NSA tool to get BLM protesters' emails, text messages
description_short: Trump: FBI abuses NSA tool to get BLM protesters' emails, text messages
description_medium: A report alleged that the FBI queried a Section 702 intelligence database for communications belonging to people arrested at Black Lives Matter protests. The searches, their authorization, and any oversight findings have not been identified, leaving the alleged violation unverified. Without those details, it cannot establish that the searches violated intelligence law.

title: Trump: White House orders gov't to continue Trump's budget plans for 2022
description_short: Trump: White House orders gov't to continue Trump's budget plans for 2022
description_medium: After the 2020 election, the White House budget office told federal agencies to continue preparing the Trump administration’s fiscal 2022 budget proposal, despite Trump’s scheduled departure before its usual February release. The instruction carried planning work into the transition. The incoming administration and Congress could revise or reject the proposal.
description_long: After the 2020 election, the White House budget office instructed federal agencies to continue preparing a Trump administration proposal for fiscal year 2022, which ran from October 2021 through September 2022. The direction came before Trump was scheduled to leave office and ahead of the proposal’s customary February release. Continuing the drafting process could carry the outgoing administration’s priorities into the transition documents, but a presidential budget proposal is not binding. The incoming administration could revise or replace it, and Congress would decide whether to enact funding. It is unclear whether agencies completed the draft or how much, if any, appeared in the next administration’s budget proposal. The event documents an instruction to keep working on a future budget during a contested transition, not control over the eventual spending plan. Agencies could keep drafting under the outgoing administration’s direction until the next president set new priorities.
organization_tags: White House Office of Management and Budget
